problem: LLMs hallucinate on domain-specific and reasoning-heavy tasks; plain RAG and retrieval of redundant triplets give the LLM noisy or unordered evidence for multi-hop KGQA.
method: GraphRAG-style SG-RAG: use Cypher queries to search a KG and retrieve the necessary subgraph, then a Merging and Ordering Triplets (MOT) step hierarchically merges retrieved subgraphs to reduce triplet redundancy and orders triplets by BFS traversal before LLM answer generation.
key_assumptions: A retrieved subgraph plus ordered triplets is sufficient context for the LLM to answer multi-hop questions.
Redundancy reduction (merging up to some point) and BFS ordering improve LLM answer precision.
MetaQA (movies domain) is representative of multi-hop KGQA. [abstract]
main_contribution: Extends SG-RAG with a Merging and Ordering Triplets step that reduces retrieved-subgraph redundancy and orders triplets by BFS, improving multi-hop answer accuracy over Chain-of-Thought and Graph Chain-of-Thought on MetaQA.
metrics: Answer accuracy (exact metric not stated in the abstract)
results: SG-RAG MOT provides more accurate answers than Chain-of-Thought and Graph Chain-of-Thought on MetaQA; merging overlapping subgraphs (up to a point) and ordering triplets helps the LLM generate more precise answers.
limitations: Retrieval and ordering happen at inference only; no fine-tuning, no supervision-design ablation, and no repair loop.
Only MetaQA is reported in the abstract; hop-depth breakdown and error analysis not stated in the abstract.
code_availability: Not stated in the abstract (no code URL in the retrieved record).

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: SG-RAG MOT retrieves and orders a context subgraph at inference time to condition an untrained LLM; the idea instead bakes same-passage context triples into the training supervision signal of a fine-tuned LLM and adds repair and RL. Both posit that surrounding triples (and their ordering/number) matter for multi-hop QA, but only the idea studies supervision regimes and iterative training.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.6 because both target multi-hop KGQA with subgraph context for an LLM; method overlap 0.4 because subgraph/triplet context construction is shared in spirit but SG-RAG MOT is a retrieval+prompting pipeline with no SFT, SFT-regime comparison, repair, or RL; evaluation overlap 0.5 because both use multi-hop QA accuracy, but on different benchmarks (MetaQA vs the idea's open/undetermined setting).
